title: Check inherited contribution policy before research intake
applies_when: Adding a public repository to an automated contribution scout, especially when a clone contains no CONTRIBUTING file, AI/human-review rules depend on contributor status, or a technically valid fix may not be publishable.
lesson: Check contributor eligibility before expensive discovery, then recheck before publication. GitHub can inherit rules from the owner's public .github repository, absent from the target clone. Resolve the effective document using its actual public html_url repository, pin and read it; follow linked policies too. Keep technical correctness, contributor-policy eligibility and current interaction permissions separate. Pallets' linked AI policy specifically excludes AI use by new contributors; established contributors still need genuine personal understanding and authorship, not an agent-issued trust certificate. Tests or a review checkbox do not override such a restriction. The repository metadata GET can cheaply expose archived/disabled state and PR creation policy: has_pull_requests=true does not override collaborators_only. An existing public fork is not an upstream PR. Temporary interaction limits and per-user PR caps are additional, separate constraints. Preserve useful private evidence, respect existing authors' patches, and redirect contribution effort instead of bypassing a restriction.
avoid_when: An absent profile/file, missing setting or failed read is not permission. Settings are timestamped observations, not contributor authorization; all does not prove an available per-user quota or permissive written rules. A prior contributor's reported denial is a reason to investigate, not proof that every user remains restricted. Limits can expire and policies can change. Do not transfer an organization's policy elsewhere, infer eligibility from keywords, or treat disclosure/review requirements as blanket bans. Internal reference testing does not authorize externally submitting its AI-generated output. A PR restriction does not by itself forbid bug reports; review the actual issue policy independently. No PR-yield or cost benefit is established by this lesson.

evidence.note: GitHub documents default community files in the owner's .github repository, their location precedence and why inherited files are not present in individual clones.

The linked policy covers all community interactions, distinguishes new from established trusted contributors, and requires genuine personal understanding and creation. Recheck this live policy before deciding eligibility; do not simplify it to a universal rule for every project or contributor.
GitHub documents temporary interaction restrictions, including collaborator-only participation that can prevent creating PRs independently of a project's written contribution guide.
GitHub separately supports disabling PRs and restricting their creation to collaborators; enabled features and written contribution guides are not a complete access decision.

A release-reproduced concurrency bug has a tested public fork but no upstream PR because creation is collaborators-only. It was submitted through the independently permitted issue channel, not counted as a PR conversion.
